## 1

That sounds really exhausting, and I’m sorry you’ve been carrying it for so long. Before you make a final decision tomorrow, could we talk tonight or tomorrow morning about what’s been happening? You don’t have to keep suffering, but it might help to look at your options—taking a day off, speaking with your manager or HR, or lining up another job—so you can leave in a way that protects you financially and emotionally. Whatever you decide, I’m here with you.

## 2

I understand why some space images can seem suspicious—many are processed, stitched together, or enhanced for scientific reasons. But the idea that all of them are fake doesn’t fit the huge amount of independent evidence. People can observe Earth’s curved shadow during lunar eclipses, track satellites, use GPS, communicate with spacecraft, and watch ships disappear over the horizon. Space agencies, private companies, universities, and observers in many countries all collect compatible data. You don’t have to trust one photograph; the evidence comes from many different methods that agree with one another.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors, like the colors in a rainbow. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny molecules in the air. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more easily than most other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from across the sky.

Violet light scatters even more, but our eyes are less sensitive to violet, and some violet light is absorbed high in the atmosphere. That is why the sky usually looks blue to us. At sunset, sunlight travels through much more atmosphere, scattering away much of the blue and leaving more red, orange, and pink light.

## 4

雨落在深夜的城市里，像无数细小的手指，轻轻敲打着窗玻璃。街灯被水汽晕成一团昏黄的光，积水倒映着摇晃的树影和偶尔驶过的车灯。远处传来轮胎碾过路面的声响，短暂而空旷。屋檐下，一只流浪猫蜷缩着躲雨，湿漉漉的耳朵不时抖动。屋内的钟声缓慢走过十二点，热茶的雾气模糊了窗外。整个夜晚安静得像一场未醒的梦，只有雨还在不停地说着什么。
